questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Always feel the doors first to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials warning placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
Hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire needs special training and gear. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you have the right equipment and training.

questions.question: Which task is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put the fire out on your own.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put the fire out on your own.
questions.explanation: Your jobs are to keep people away, limit spills if safe, inform emergency responders of dangers, and give them shipping papers. Do not fight hazardous materials fires yourself unless you have proper equipment and training.

questions.question: Which sign shows cargo may contain hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often hold and transport hazardous materials. Packaging type can show whether materials are hazardous.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous materials placards?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, how can you best learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual is a first step. Learn more by reading federal and state rules about hazardous materials transport and by taking hazardous materials training courses.

questions.question: What do you need from a shipper to accept a package with hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Shippers certify that packages are prepared correctly. You can accept this certification unless the package looks unsafe or doesn't follow the rules.

questions.question: Many poisonous products are also:
questions.explanation: Many poisonous hazardous materials are also flammable.

questions.question: How should a trailer be cleaned after corrosive materials leak inside?

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Parts exposed to corrosive liquids must be washed thoroughly with water.

questions.question: Where should shipping papers be placed?

options.text: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Easy to see for anyone entering the cab.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be easy to see for anyone entering the cab. Keep them in a pouch on the driver's door or another place the driver can reach while wearing a seat belt.

questions.question: When can you leave a vehicle carrying explosives unattended?

options.text: On the shoulder of a highway.

questions.explanation: You may only leave a vehicle with explosives unattended in a safe haven. A safe haven is an approved location for parking vehicles loaded with explosives.

questions.question: What is required when transporting explosives?
questions.explanation: You must follow a written route plan when transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives. Avoid busy areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Check for any route restrictions.

questions.question: How far must you park from any building when carrying Division 1.1 explosives?
questions.explanation: Do not park within 300 feet of a bridge, tunnel, building, crowded area, or open fire when carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives.

questions.question: What should you do if hazardous materials are leaking from your vehicle?

options.text: Keep driving to find a phone to call the National Response Center.
Leave the area to get help.

questions.explanation: Park your vehicle as soon as possible if you see hazardous materials leaking. Continuing to drive spreads contamination, creates danger, and increases cleanup costs.

questions.question: How should you load hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat sources. Regulations prohibit explosives and flammable materials from being loaded in spaces with heaters.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's ID number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging and shipping papers. It must also appear on cargo tanks and other bulk packaging.

questions.question: What should you do with the engine when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling. Someone must always stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow while refueling.

questions.question: How many identical placards must a vehicle have?
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have four identical placards: one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: What placard is needed if "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on shipping papers or packaging, use the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: If you find leaking cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Touch the leaking material to find out what it is.
Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
Assume all the cargo is leaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use shipping papers and labels to identify the leaking cargo.
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, identify the material using shipping papers, labels, or the package location. Do not touch the leaking material.

questions.question: Which material may need a transport index?
questions.explanation: Some radioactive materials need a transport index. This number shows how much control the material needs during transport. The total transport index of all cargo in one vehicle cannot be more than 50.

questions.question: What is the minimum fire extinguisher rating for a placarded vehicle's engine?
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's engine must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: How should a driver warn others about hazardous materials?

options.text: Use HazMat placards on the truck.
Use flashing lights on the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use HazMat placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Drivers must display diamond-shaped warning signs called placards on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Shippers must provide placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: When must the National Response Center be notified about an incident?

options.text: When someone needs to be hospitalized.
When someone is injured but not hospitalized.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is injured but not hospitalized.
questions.explanation: The National Response Center must be notified of death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, evacuation of the public, closure of a major route for more than one hour, or fires and spills involving radiation, bacteria, or toxins. A driver can also report if they think the situation is serious.

questions.question: Who must label hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials. The shipper must also supply the warning placards.

questions.question: If your vehicle with explosives breaks down, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: Stand on the road and wave your arms.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use reflective triangles or red electric lights to warn others. Never use burning signals like flares or fuses with explosives.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: When loading corrosive liquids by hand, load breakable containers one at a time. Keep them upright. Do not drop or roll the containers.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 materials cannot be in a trailer with:
questions.explanation: Cargo heaters are not always allowed. When transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gases), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials, heaters in the same space are generally prohibited.
